summary.intent: Execute Phase 27 of the cipher-box project to implement a writable shares proof-of-concept, covering API backend, owner UI, and recipient UI for write-enabled folder sharing.
summary.outcome: All 3 plans executed and verified, 12 security issues fixed via TDD, 21 E2E tests written and passing, PR #372 created and all 20 review threads resolved across 3 rounds of CodeRabbit feedback.

repo: SDK packages (core, sdk-core, sdk) must be built before the web dev server can start — `@cipherbox/sdk` resolution fails otherwise
`.env` files are not committed to cipher-box-ci-debug; they must be copied from the cipher-box checkout when setting up a new dev environment
Web app health check falls back to `window.location.origin + '/api'` when `VITE_API_URL` is unset, which resolves to port 5173 instead of 3000 — always set VITE_API_URL in web .env

Two conflicting `RequestWithUser` types existed: a local one in auth.controller.ts extending NestJS `@nestjs/common` Request (Fetch API), and the canonical one in common/types.ts extending Express Request — the local one was wrong
`createFileMetadata` zeroes the IPNS private key internally after wrapping, so callers cannot retrieve the raw key after calling it — must inline keypair generation when dual-wrapping is needed

The `withConflictRetry` closures in `useSharedNavigation.ts` captured stale React state for `currentSequenceNumber` and `folderChildren` — navigation functions (`navigateToSubfolder`, `navigateUp`, `navigateToBreadcrumb`) were also missing ref sync, causing stale data after navigation preceding a write
NestJS `api:generate` script runs ESLint across the entire repo, so pre-existing lint errors in unrelated files (sdk-e2e) cause it to fail even when the OpenAPI spec was successfully generated
The GSD workflow uses `gsd-tools.cjs` CLI for all state/roadmap/commit operations — direct git commits bypass tracking and should use the tool instead
API client must be regenerated after every DTO change that affects the OpenAPI spec; `@ApiProperty` enum decorators are what drive the spec, not just runtime validation
IpnsService injecting SharesService created a circular-like dependency that broke the ipns.service.spec.ts test module — mock must be explicitly provided

code.finding: Checks `item.fileMetaIpnsName` which is empty string for files uploaded via shared folders (set at useSharedNavigation.ts:807) — causes 'File metadata IPNS name not available' error for all shared-upload files

Original shared upload set `fileMetaIpnsName: ''` because it used `createFileMetadata` which zeroes keys internally — fixed by inlining IPNS keypair generation with dual-key wrapping (owner in FilePointer, recipient in share_keys with keyType 'file-ipns')
`handleUpdateFile` did not re-wrap the new file key for share recipients after updating file content — owner edits silently broke recipient access until `reWrapForRecipients` was added post-update
Permission downgrade (write→read) needed to be wrapped in a transaction — `encryptedIpnsKey` nullification and `file-ipns` share_key deletion could diverge on partial failure
Guards `&& existing.userId === userId` already existed on TEE enrollment and DB update paths — write-share recipients cannot overwrite TEE enrollment config (H-01 was already implemented)

Subfolder key wrapping used the recipient's public key instead of the owner's — owner permanently lost access to subfolders created by recipients until fixed to wrap with ownerPublicKey in FilePointer and add recipient share_key separately
`setUpgradingId` was set before early returns at lines 374/380 with no finally block — UI would get stuck in busy state if permission upgrade failed before the try block
ECIES ciphertext hex validation used `@Matches(/^[0-9a-f]+$/i)` but not even-length enforcement — ECIES output is always even-length bytes-as-hex; pattern should be `^([0-9a-f]{2})+$`

workflow: Dev servers started as background tasks get killed when conversation context resets — use detached processes (`nohup ... &` or similar) for servers that need to outlive the task
TDD red-green cycle for security fixes: stash partial fixes, write failing tests against broken code, pop stash, verify tests go green — produces cleaner audit trail than retrofitting tests
Security reviews should be run immediately after implementing crypto features before moving to E2E testing — 12 issues caught that would have been harder to fix post-merge
E2E test selector bugs are inevitable when writing tests without running them — always run the full suite locally before committing; expect 2-3 selector fix rounds
Playwright test failures on `.navigateBack()` for deeply nested paths need explicit `waitForURL` calls rather than chained back navigations with timeouts
Coverage thresholds (78% branch) can be knocked below by new untested branches — check `pnpm test --coverage` locally before pushing security/backend changes
When resolving PR review threads, reply to the comment ID (not thread ID) via REST, then resolve the thread via GraphQL — these are two separate operations

friction: Background tasks killed by conversation context shifts repeatedly knocked down dev servers mid-UAT session — had to restart 5+ times across the session
DB host IP changed (192.168.133.114 → 192.168.133.12) mid-session with no .env in the CI debug checkout — required creating .env from scratch before API could start
Git lock file left behind by a previous operation blocked commits — had to manually remove
API client regeneration is a mandatory but error-prone step after every DTO change — easy to forget, causes TypeScript errors downstream
The `api:generate` script lints the entire repo, so pre-existing errors in unrelated files (sdk-e2e) caused false failures during client regeneration
GitHub API GraphQL queries for PR threads timed out repeatedly, requiring multiple retry attempts
The IpnsService circular dependency fix required updating the test module to provide a `SharesService` mock — CI caught this after a clean local run
Two rounds of CI failures post-PR creation (test DI failure, then lint unused import) that passed locally due to different module resolution
open_items: File upload to shared folders only creates `file-ipns` share_keys for the uploading recipient — if multiple recipients have write access, only the uploader can open the file they uploaded (PoC limitation)

`reWrapForRecipients` in useFileOperations.ts does not re-wrap `file-ipns` type keys when owner edits a file — owner edits will break access for recipients who uploaded the file (noted as 'by design' in review but is a real gap post-PoC)
Received shares polling fetches all shares every 30s but only checks the first 100 — pagination not implemented (PoC limitation)
The `(mockShareRepo as any).manager` cast in shares.service.spec.ts is the last remaining `no-explicit-any` warning — requires TypeORM EntityManager typing improvements to fix cleanly
Pre-existing TypeScript errors in `tests/sdk-e2e/src/suites/error-cases.test.ts` were not addressed — should be cleaned up in a separate pass
E2E tests for writable shares (21 tests) only run locally — CI pipeline does not yet execute the web-e2e Playwright suite against a real stack
Silent revocation (403 → RO transition) and 30s polling detection of permission changes are tested in unit/E2E specs but not verified in human UAT during this session
